title: Questions to Ask During an Initial Architect Consultation in Scarsdale
excerpt: Planning a renovation or addition in Scarsdale? Here are the key questions to ask your architect at your first meeting to make sure the project stays on track and matches your vision.
content:
You've decided it's time to renovate your Scarsdale home or add square footage. You call an architect. Now what? The first consultation sets the tone for everything that follows. If you walk in unprepared, you might miss critical information. If you ask the right questions upfront, you'll know exactly what to expect and whether this architect is the right fit for your project.

The best conversation happens when you come ready with a list. You don't need pages of notes, but knowing what matters to you makes the meeting productive. Here's what you should cover.

Who Will Actually Run Your Project?

This is the first thing to ask. When you hire a licensed architect in Westchester, NY, you want to know if that person will be on your job every step of the way. Some firms assign you to a junior architect or project manager. Others have architects who oversee multiple projects at once and show up sporadically.

At House Architecture & Construction, PLLC, the principal architect runs every single project personally. That matters. You're not working with a middle person or a rotating team. The same person who listens to your ideas at the first meeting is the one solving problems during construction and ensuring quality control. Ask your architect directly if they'll be the person you see throughout the project.

Do They Also Hold a General Contractor License?

There's real value in working with someone who understands both sides. A residential architect in Scarsdale who is also a licensed general contractor knows how buildings actually go together. They understand what's buildable, what's realistic, and how costs play out in the field. They don't design things that contractors later tell you won't work or will cost twice as much as expected.

When architecture and contracting are in one person's hands, communication is clearer. There's no gap between the drawings and the execution. Ask if your architect carries a general contractor license in New York and whether they personally oversee construction.

What's Your Experience with Scarsdale Permits and the Building Department?

Every Westchester municipality has its own building department and permit process. Scarsdale is no different. Your architect should be familiar with what the Scarsdale Building Department wants to see. They should know the typical timeline, the submission requirements, and the common questions that come up.

Ask how many projects they've done in Scarsdale recently. Ask what the current review times look like. A general contractor in Westchester who has worked in this town for years has built relationships with the inspectors and knows how to submit plans that move through the system efficiently.

Can You Handle the Scope I Have in Mind?

Be clear about what you want. Are you doing a kitchen remodel? A second-story addition? A complete historic restoration? An open-concept conversion? A design-build in Westchester can tackle all of these, but you need an architect who has actually done what you're trying to do.

Ask to see examples of similar work. Ask how they handled challenges. Ask if they've worked with your home's style before. The more specific you are about your project, the better answer you'll get.

What Happens Next?

By the end of the consultation, you should know the next steps, the timeline, and what you need to prepare. You should feel like someone listened to you and understands your home.
